evals.name: cuts-scope-no-goal-needs
evals.prompt: Our 3-person support team wants the weekly list of closed tickets as a CSV so they can paste it into a spreadsheet they already maintain. Right now they ask engineering every Friday. My plan: build a reporting service with a plugin system for export formats (CSV, XLSX, PDF), a scheduler for recurring exports, per-user export templates, and an S3 archive of every export ever generated. Goal: support gets the weekly CSV without asking engineering. Constraint: it has to ship this sprint, and I'm the only engineer on it.
evals.expected_output: The first round proposes cutting the scope no goal needs and recommends the smallest export that gets support their weekly CSV on their own.
assertions: Proposes cutting at least two of: the plugin system, XLSX/PDF formats, per-user templates, the S3 archive, tying each cut to no stated goal or constraint needing it.
Recommends an approach no bigger than a single CSV export support can get on their own, such as a button, a saved query, or one scheduled email.
Asks no design-detail question about scope it has not first established is needed, such as PDF layout, template schema, or archive retention.
Introduces no new area of scope that neither the plan nor a stated goal or constraint raises; every question settles a goal or constraint, or decides on scope the plan proposed or the goal needs.

evals.name: keeps-what-a-constraint-requires
evals.prompt: Adding password reset to our B2B app. Goal: users can reset a forgotten password without contacting support. Constraint: our SOC 2 audit next quarter requires reset tokens to be single-use, expire within 15 minutes, and every reset to be audit-logged. Plan: an emailed reset link, plus SMS reset and security questions as backup options. To ship faster I'm thinking of skipping the audit log for v1.
evals.expected_output: The first round keeps the audit log and token rules the SOC 2 constraint requires, and proposes cutting the backup reset paths no goal needs.
assertions: Recommends keeping the audit log for v1, citing the SOC 2 constraint, rather than endorsing skipping it.
Proposes no relaxation of single-use reset tokens or their 15-minute expiry, treating both as fixed by the SOC 2 constraint.
Proposes cutting SMS reset and security questions as serving no stated goal or constraint, leaving the emailed link as the only v1 reset path.
Introduces no new area of scope that neither the plan nor a stated goal or constraint raises; every question settles a goal or constraint, or decides on scope the plan proposed or the goal needs.

evals.name: settles-goals-first
evals.prompt: I think we should rewrite our internal admin dashboard in a newer frontend framework.
evals.expected_output: The first round settles what the rewrite must achieve and what constrains it, and keeps a smaller change than a full rewrite on the table until those are known.
assertions: Asks in the first round what the rewrite must achieve, the problem or goal behind it.
Asks in the first round what constraints apply, such as time, people, or what must keep working.
Defers framework choice and migration-detail questions until the goals are settled, rather than asking them in the first round.
Raises a smaller change than a full rewrite, such as fixing the specific pain points in place or migrating incrementally, as a candidate answer.
Introduces no new area of scope that neither the plan nor a stated goal or constraint raises; every question settles a goal or constraint, or decides on scope the plan proposed or the goal needs.
